quercetin induces MUC2 secretion and MUC2 and 5AC gene expression through PLC/PKC/ERK1/2 pathway in intestinal goblet cell-like LS174T cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the main dietary flavonoids, quercetin and kaempferol, exert a protective action against intestinal inflammation and fibrosis by modulating the secretion of mucin, the major component of the mucus barrier, via the activation of PLC/PKC/ERK1/2 signaling pathway.

quercetin, a natural flavonoid present in many foods, increases MUC2 and/or MUC5AC gene expression and secretion in intestinal goblet cell line LS174T and in enterocyte line Caco 2, through the activation of PLC/PKCa and ERK1/2 signaling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flavonoid querecetin induces the secretion of mucin by goblet cells, and the gene expression in both goblet cells and in enterocytes.

quercetin may be a potential therapeutic tool for the treatment of gastrointestinal diseases characterized by a reduction in the secretion of mucin by goblet cells and/or in enterocytes, such as inflammatory bowel diseases, celiac disease and colon cancer.
